epithet: The case for One God, argued whole
lede: There is hardly a law in it. From its first word of praise to its last, this surah does one thing: it argues — with the sky, the grain splitting in the earth, the soul taken in sleep and returned at dawn — that there is no god but Allah. More than forty times it hands the Prophet ﷺ his answer in a single word: Say.

names.name: al-Anʿām
names.note: After the livestock around which the idolaters had built their taboos and their offerings (6:136–144) — rules they ascribed to Allah, and which the surah takes apart one by one.

revelation.detail: Mujāhid relates from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is among what came down in Makkah, and that is the saying of al-Ḥasan, Qatādah and Jābir ibn Zayd; al-Qurṭubī calls it the saying of the greater number. Reports from Ibn ʿAbbās except between two and six ayat as Madinan, among them “They did not esteem Allah as He deserves” (6:91) and the three ayat of the commandments (6:151–153). The traditional order places it fifty-fifth.

evidence.quote: رَوى مُجاهِدٌ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ: أنَّ ( الأنْعامَ ) مِمّا نَزَلَ بِمَكَّةَ. وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، وقَتادَةَ، وجابِرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ
سُورَةُ الْأَنْعَامِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْأَكْثَرِينَ

attested.quote: سُورَةُ الْأَنْعَامِ مَكِّيَّةٌ، وَهِيَ مِائَةٌ وَخَمْسٌ وَسِتُّونَ آيَةً
أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ وأبُو الشَّيْخِ، وابْنُ مَرْدَوَيْهِ والبَيْهَقِيُّ في الدَّلائِلِ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةُ الأنْعامِ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, Abū al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

attested.quote: قالَ الثَّعْلَبِيُّ: سُورَةُ الأنْعامِ مَكِّيَّةٌ إلّا سِتَّ آياتٍ نَزَلَتْ بِالمَدِينَةِ
attested.says: Citing al-Thaʿlabī: Makkan, except six ayat that came down in Madinah.

setting: By the later years in Makkah the argument had hardened. Quraysh no longer asked what the message was; they asked for a spectacle to prove it — an angel sent down, a book on parchment they could touch — and meanwhile held to a religion in which Allah was acknowledged as Creator and then given partners in everything that mattered. This surah meets that position head on, and it has two ways of speaking that it alternates from start to finish.

The first is to describe. “He it is who created you from clay.” “With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. He knows what is on the land and in the sea; not a leaf falls but He knows it.” “He it is who takes your souls by night.” “Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone.” “Vision does not encompass Him, but He encompasses all vision.” The second is to dictate. “Say: to whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth? Say: to Allah.” “Say: shall I take as protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who feeds and is not fed?” “Say: what thing is greatest in testimony? Say: Allah.”

At its centre it tells how Ibrāhīm reasoned with his people. Night fell and he saw a star: “This is my lord.” It set: “I do not love things that set.” Then the moon, then the sun, and each went down. “My people, I am free of what you associate. I have turned my face to Him who originated the heavens and the earth.” Eighteen prophets are then named in four ayat, and the Prophet ﷺ is told: “Those are the ones whom Allah guided; so follow their guidance.”

The human cost of the argument is here too. The chiefs of Quraysh told him to send away the poor men who sat around him, so that such people should not grow bold with them. Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who was one of them, says there were six that day — himself, Ibn Masʿūd, Bilāl, a man of Hudhayl and two others — and that the ayah came down: “Do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face.”

Only near the end does it come to the cattle: this animal’s back forbidden, that one’s milk reserved for men, a share of the crop for the idols — and, in the same breath, the killing of children. Ibn ʿAbbās said: if you would like to know how ignorant the Arabs were, read what comes after the hundred and thirtieth ayah of al-Anʿām. Against that invented law the surah sets Allah’s own, in three ayat that begin: “Say: come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you.”

occasions.title: “Do not drive them away”
occasions.text: Saʿd said: “We were six men with the Prophet ﷺ, and the idolaters said to him: ‘Drive these away, so that they do not grow bold with us.’ There were myself, Ibn Masʿūd, a man of Hudhayl, Bilāl, and two men I shall not name. There came into the mind of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what Allah willed should come, and he thought it over. Then Allah sent down: ‘Do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face.’”

occasions.title: “Which of us has not wronged himself?”
occasions.text: When “Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrong” came down, it weighed on the Companions, and they said: “Which of us has not wronged himself?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is not as you think. It is only as Luqmān said to his son: ‘My son, do not associate partners with Allah; association is a tremendous wrong.’”
occasions.source: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: al-Bukhārī (4629) and Muslim (124).

occasions.title: “What Allah kills, you will not eat?”
occasions.text: Some people came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “Messenger of Allah, are we to eat what we kill, and not eat what Allah kills?” Then Allah sent down: “So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you believe in His ayat,” to His saying: “if you were to obey them, you would be idolaters.”
occasions.source: Ibn ʿAbbās: al-Tirmidhī (3069); ṣaḥīḥ according to al-Albānī.

aim: To establish the creed of tawḥīd by rational proofs, and to demolish the beliefs of idolatry.
themes: Ibrāhīm’s argument from the setting stars
The signs in grain, rain and night

outline.title: Praise, and those who turn away
outline.summary: Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve set up equals to their Lord. He it is who created you from clay, then decreed a term. No sign comes to them of the signs of their Lord but they turn from it. They say, “Why has no angel been sent down to him?” Had We sent down to you a book on parchment and they touched it with their hands, they would have said, “This is plain magic.” Say: travel in the land and see how the deniers ended.

outline.title: To whom does it all belong?
outline.summary: Say: to whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth? Say: to Allah; He has prescribed mercy upon Himself. Say: shall I take a protector other than Allah, who feeds and is not fed? If Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but He. Say: what thing is greatest in testimony? Say: Allah. If you could see when they are stood before the Fire and say, “Would that we were sent back.” The life of this world is nothing but play and diversion.

outline.title: We know it grieves you
outline.summary: We know that what they say grieves you; yet it is not you they deny — it is the ayat of Allah the wrongdoers reject. There is no creature on the earth, nor bird flying on its wings, but they are communities like you. Say: tell me, if Allah’s punishment came to you, would you call on other than Allah? Do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening. When those who believe in Our ayat come to you, say: “Peace be upon you; your Lord has prescribed mercy upon Himself.”

outline.title: The keys of the unseen
outline.summary: With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. Not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth. He it is who takes your souls by night, and knows what you earned by day. Say: who rescues you from the darknesses of land and sea? Say: He is able to send punishment upon you from above you or from beneath your feet. Leave those who take their religion as play. The Day He says “Be,” and it is.

outline.title: Ibrāhīm, and the guided
outline.summary: Thus We showed Ibrāhīm the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. When night covered him he saw a star: “This is my lord.” When it set, he said: “I do not love things that set.” Then the moon; then the sun. “I have turned my face to Him who originated the heavens and the earth.” Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrong — theirs is security. We gave him Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb; and Nūḥ before; and of his descendants Dāwūd, Sulaymān, Ayyūb, Yūsuf, Mūsā and Hārūn… Those are the ones whom Allah guided; so follow their guidance.

outline.title: Signs for those who look
outline.summary: They did not esteem Allah as He deserves when they said, “Allah has sent down nothing to any human being.” This is a blessed Book We have sent down. Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone; He brings the living from the dead. He made the stars for you to be guided by. He sends down water, and brings out green shoots, clustered grain, palms, vines, olives and pomegranates. Originator of the heavens and the earth — how could He have a son? Vision does not encompass Him, but He encompasses all vision (6:103). Do not revile those they call upon besides Allah.

outline.title: Guidance is His
outline.summary: Even if We sent down the angels to them, and the dead spoke to them, they would not believe unless Allah willed. For every prophet We made an enemy. Shall I seek a judge other than Allah? If you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray. Eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned. Is one who was dead, and We gave him life and made for him a light to walk by among people, like one in darknesses? Whomever Allah wills to guide, He opens his chest to Islam.

outline.title: The cattle, and the invented law
outline.summary: They assign to Allah a share of the crops and cattle He created, and say, “This is for Allah” — so they claim — “and this for our partners.” Their partners made the killing of their children seem fair to many idolaters. They say, “These cattle and crops are forbidden.” Lost are those who killed their children in folly. Eight pairs: has He forbidden the two males, or the two females? Say: I find nothing forbidden in what is revealed to me, except carrion, blood poured out, and the flesh of swine. They will say: “Had Allah willed, we would not have associated.” Say: Allah’s is the conclusive argument.

outline.title: The commandments, and the close
outline.summary: Say: come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him; be good to parents; do not kill your children from poverty; do not approach indecencies; do not kill the soul Allah has forbidden; do not approach the orphan’s property; give full measure; when you speak, be just; fulfil the covenant of Allah. This is My path, straight; so follow it. Whoever brings a good deed will have ten like it. Say: my prayer and my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds (6:162). No soul bears the burden of another.

keyAyah.why: The surah’s last “Say” but one, and the conclusion of its whole argument: if He alone creates, then all of a life — its worship and its end — is His.

virtues.text: “The keys of the unseen are five: ‘With Allah is the knowledge of the Hour; He sends down the rain; He knows what is in the wombs; no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow; and no soul knows in what land it will die.’”

When this ayah came down — “Say: He is able to send punishment upon you from above you” — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I seek refuge in Your Face.” “Or from beneath your feet” — he said: “I seek refuge in Your Face.” “Or to confound you in factions and make some of you taste the violence of others” — he said: “This is lighter,” or “This is easier.”

“The Hour will not come until the sun rises from its place of setting. When it rises and the people see it, they will all believe — and that is when ‘no soul will benefit from its faith, if it had not believed before.’”

Ibn ʿAbbās said: “If it would please you to know the ignorance of the Arabs, read what comes after the hundred and thirtieth ayah of Sūrat al-Anʿām: ‘Lost are those who killed their children in folly, without knowledge.’”

before: Al-Māʾidah ended: “To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is in them.” Al-Anʿām opens: “Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth.”
after: Al-Anʿām argues for tawḥīd from creation. Al-Aʿrāf argues it from history: what became of each people who were called to it and refused.
